1.explanation: FormGroup.js declares the `legendText` prop type as `PropTypes.string` and only renders simple strings in its legend. To support passing JSX (like a Tooltip node), this file must be updated to accept `PropTypes.node` (or `oneOfType([PropTypes.string, PropTypes.node])`). FormGroup-test.js covers the legendText rendering and will need its expectations updated (or additional tests added) to allow passing and correctly rendering React nodes in the legend.
1.bug_scenario: When you wrap the FormGroup legendText in a React node (for example a Tooltip component) instead of a plain string, you get a prop‐type warning “Invalid prop `legendText` of type `object` supplied to `FormGroup`, expected `string`.” In other words FormGroup only accepts string legends today and cannot render embedded components (icons, tooltips, links, etc.) in its legend text.

2.explanation:
1. FormGroup.js – this is where `legendText` is defined in `propTypes` as `PropTypes.string`. It also renders the legend by interpolating `legendText` directly. Changing the propType to `PropTypes.node` (and ensuring the output supports JSX) allows the component to accept and render React elements like `<Tooltip>`.
2. FormGroup-test.js – the existing tests/snapshots assume a string legend. They will need to be updated (or new tests added) to verify that passing a node (e.g. a tooltip wrapper) does not produce warnings and renders correctly. This ensures the new `PropTypes.node` support is validated in the test suite.
2.bug_scenario: In the default Carbon React `FormGroup`, the `legendText` prop is currently typed and treated as a plain string, so passing a React element (e.g. a `<Tooltip>` around the label text) produces a prop‐type warning and doesn’t render the embedded tooltip. The user wants to wrap the legend text in a `<Tooltip>` (an object/JSX node) rather than just supply a string.
